simple_definition: A machine that follows instructions to take in, change, keep and show information.
technical_definition: A programmable electronic device that executes stored instructions to process data received as input, retain results in storage and present output.
example: A laptop, a phone, a cash machine.

simple_definition: The physical parts of a computer.
technical_definition: The tangible components of a computing system, such as the processor, memory, storage devices, display and network adapter.

simple_definition: The part that carries out instructions.
technical_definition: The central processing unit: the hardware component that executes program instructions.
example: The chip that runs your browser's instructions.

simple_definition: Fast, temporary working space that is emptied when the power goes off.
technical_definition: Random-access memory: volatile, fast storage used for the data and instructions a computer is currently using.
example: The words you have typed but not yet saved.

simple_definition: Slower, permanent space that keeps information when the power is off.
technical_definition: Non-volatile data storage, such as a solid-state drive or hard disk, that retains data without power.

simple_definition: A unit for measuring stored information; enough for one English letter.
technical_definition: A unit of digital information made of eight bits.
example: The word 'Hi' takes two bytes in simple text.

simple_definition: Instructions that tell hardware what to do.
technical_definition: Programs and data that direct the operation of hardware.

simple_definition: Software that does a specific job for a person.
technical_definition: A program designed to perform a task for a user, running on top of an operating system.
example: A text editor, a browser, Git.

simple_definition: The main software that manages the computer, its files and the other programs.
technical_definition: System software that manages hardware resources, provides services such as file storage and process scheduling, and hosts applications.

simple_definition: A file or program that puts an application on your computer.
technical_definition: A program or package that copies an application's files to the correct locations and registers it with the operating system.
example: A Git setup file downloaded from the maker's site.

simple_definition: An account or permission level allowed to change the computer's system settings.
technical_definition: A privileged user role that may modify system-wide configuration and install software for all users.
example: The prompt that asks whether to allow an installer to make changes.

simple_definition: A program that installs and updates applications from a trusted collection.
technical_definition: A tool that resolves, retrieves, installs, updates and removes software packages from configured repositories.

simple_definition: A named collection of information kept in storage.
technical_definition: A named sequence of bytes stored in a file system, with associated metadata.

simple_definition: Information about a file, such as its size, dates, owner and permissions.
technical_definition: Attributes a file system records about a file separately from the file's contents.
example: The size and last-changed date shown in a detailed listing.

simple_definition: The letters after the last dot in a file name; a label for the kind of contents.
technical_definition: A suffix of a file name, conventionally indicating the file's format; it does not change the contents.

simple_definition: A container that holds files and other folders.
technical_definition: A file-system object that contains references to files and other directories.

simple_definition: The folder that belongs to your user account.
technical_definition: The directory assigned to a user account for that user's files and settings; often written ~ in a shell.

simple_definition: The top folder of a tree; everything else is inside it.
technical_definition: The topmost directory of a file-system hierarchy, written / on Unix-like systems.

simple_definition: A written description of where a file or folder is in the tree.
technical_definition: A sequence of directory names, separated by a separator character, identifying a location in a file system.

simple_definition: A path that starts at the root and means the same wherever you are.
technical_definition: A path that begins at the file-system root (or a drive letter on Windows) and fully specifies a location.

simple_definition: A path that starts from where you are now.
technical_definition: A path interpreted relative to the current working directory.

simple_definition: The folder that counts as 'here' when you give a relative path.
technical_definition: The directory against which a process resolves relative paths.
example: sunrise-bakery after you have moved into it.

simple_definition: A file that ordinary listings do not show unless asked.
technical_definition: A file whose name (on Unix-like systems, a leading dot) or attribute marks it to be omitted from default listings.

simple_definition: A rule about who may read, change or run a file.
technical_definition: An access-control attribute governing read, write and execute rights of users on a file or directory.

simple_definition: Information stored as ordinary characters with no fonts, colours or layout.
technical_definition: A sequence of encoded characters with no formatting metadata, stored as bytes according to a character encoding.

simple_definition: A file that is not plain text, such as a photo or a word-processor document.
technical_definition: A file whose bytes are not a sequence of characters intended to be read as text.

simple_definition: One file that holds other files in compressed form.
technical_definition: A container format that stores multiple files, optionally compressed, in a single file.
example: Many word-processor documents are ZIP archives internally.

simple_definition: A program for creating and changing plain text files.
technical_definition: An application that edits plain text without adding formatting information.
example: Any editor that saves only characters.
related: code editor; word processor; plain text

simple_definition: A program for writing formatted documents, saved in a packaged format.
technical_definition: An application that edits formatted documents, storing styles and layout along with the text, normally in a binary or packaged format.

simple_definition: A text editor with extra help for writing structured text such as software.
technical_definition: A text editor providing features such as syntax highlighting, line numbers, multi-file search and folder navigation.
example: An editor showing your project's files in a side panel.

simple_definition: Colouring parts of text according to their role so the structure is easy to see.
technical_definition: Display of tokens of structured text in different colours or styles according to their syntactic category.
example: Tags in HTML shown in one colour and words in another.

simple_definition: The folder of files that makes up one piece of work.
technical_definition: A set of files, typically under one directory, that together form a program, website, document set or tool.

simple_definition: The human-written files from which a project is made.
technical_definition: Human-readable files that specify a program, website or document set and from which deliverables are produced.

simple_definition: A text format that marks up web pages so a browser knows how to show them.
technical_definition: HyperText Markup Language: a markup language using tags to describe the structure of a web page.

simple_definition: A text format that describes how web pages look.
technical_definition: Cascading Style Sheets: a language for describing the presentation of documents written in a markup language.

simple_definition: A single unit of text: a letter, digit, symbol, emoji or space.
technical_definition: An abstract unit of written text identified by a Unicode code point.

simple_definition: The rule that turns characters into bytes and back.
technical_definition: A mapping between sequences of characters and sequences of bytes used to store or transmit text.

simple_definition: A universal list that gives every character a number.
technical_definition: A standard that assigns a unique code point to each character of the world's writing systems and many symbols.

simple_definition: The most widely used way to store Unicode text as bytes.
technical_definition: A variable-width encoding of Unicode that uses one to four bytes per character and is backward compatible with ASCII for basic English characters.
example: é is stored as the two bytes c3 a9.

simple_definition: Garbled text caused by reading with the wrong encoding.
technical_definition: Incorrect characters displayed when bytes are decoded using an encoding different from the one used to encode them.

simple_definition: The invisible character or characters that end a line of text.
technical_definition: A control character sequence marking a line break: LF on Unix-like systems, CRLF traditionally on Windows.

simple_definition: Computers connected so that they can exchange information.
technical_definition: A set of computing devices linked by communication channels.

simple_definition: The worldwide system of connected networks.
technical_definition: The global interconnection of networks that use common protocols to exchange data.
example: The connection between your laptop and a server in another country.

simple_definition: Linked pages and applications you view with a browser.
technical_definition: A system of interlinked resources, identified by URLs and transferred using HTTP, accessed with browsers over the internet.

simple_definition: An application for viewing web pages.
technical_definition: A client application that requests, interprets and displays web resources.
example: The program in which you open index.html.

simple_definition: The written address of a page or resource on the internet.
technical_definition: Uniform Resource Locator: a string that identifies a resource by scheme, host, optional port, path, optional query and optional fragment.

simple_definition: A human-friendly name, such as example.org, for a host on the internet.
technical_definition: A hierarchical name registered in the domain name system that resolves to network addresses.

simple_definition: A number that identifies a computer on a network.
technical_definition: A numeric identifier assigned to a network interface, used to route packets.

simple_definition: The internet's phone book: it turns names into numbers.
technical_definition: A distributed naming system that resolves domain names to IP addresses and other records.

simple_definition: The computer or program that asks for something.
technical_definition: The party in a client-server exchange that initiates requests.

simple_definition: A computer or program that answers requests.
technical_definition: A process (or the computer running it) that listens for and responds to requests from clients.
example: The program that sends you a web page.

simple_definition: The rules web clients and servers follow to exchange requests and replies.
technical_definition: HyperText Transfer Protocol: an application-layer protocol of requests and responses carrying methods, status codes, headers and bodies.

simple_definition: HTTP with encryption and a check of the server's identity.
technical_definition: HTTP carried over an encrypted, authenticated TLS connection.

simple_definition: On the computer you are using.
technical_definition: Residing on, or executing on, the machine at hand rather than reached over a network.
example: A file in your sharif-git-lab folder.

simple_definition: On a different computer, reached over a network.
technical_definition: Residing on another machine, accessed through a network connection.
example: A page on example.org; later, a repository on GitHub.

simple_definition: A record a service keeps to represent you.
technical_definition: A stored identity with credentials, settings and permissions maintained by a service.

simple_definition: The name that identifies your account.
technical_definition: A unique identifier for an account within a service.

simple_definition: A secret string you present to prove you own an account.
technical_definition: A memorised secret used as a credential in authentication.
example: A long passphrase of unrelated words.

simple_definition: An application that stores all your passwords securely and fills them in.
technical_definition: Software that keeps credentials in an encrypted vault protected by a master secret.
example: An app protected by one strong master password.

simple_definition: Proving who you are with two proofs from different families.
technical_definition: Authentication requiring two distinct factors: something known, something held, or something inherent.
example: Password plus a code from a phone app.

simple_definition: Proving who you are.
technical_definition: The process of verifying the identity claimed by a user or program.
example: Entering a password and a code.

simple_definition: Deciding what you are allowed to do once your identity is known.
technical_definition: The process of determining whether an authenticated identity may perform a requested action.
example: You can read a project but not delete it.

simple_definition: Giving only the access that is needed, and no more.
technical_definition: A design principle that grants a subject the minimum permissions required for its task.
example: A token that can read one project only.

simple_definition: A limited stand-in for a password; still a secret.
technical_definition: A credential string that grants specified, often time-limited, permissions to its holder.
example: A personal access token used by a tool.

simple_definition: A shareable public key and a private key that never leaves your computer.
technical_definition: A matched public/private cryptographic key pair in which data signed or locked with one key is verified or unlocked with the other.

simple_definition: A secure way to connect to another computer, which can use a key pair to prove your identity.
technical_definition: A cryptographic network protocol for secure remote login and command execution, supporting public-key authentication.
example: Connecting to a server without sending a password.

simple_definition: Tricking someone into giving away a secret by pretending to be trusted.
technical_definition: A social-engineering attack that impersonates a trusted party to obtain credentials or induce harmful actions.
example: An urgent email with a link to a lookalike site.

simple_definition: A window in which you type commands and read text replies.
technical_definition: A text-based interface (terminal emulator) through which a user interacts with a shell.
example: The Terminal application or Git Bash window.

simple_definition: The program that reads your commands and has them carried out.
technical_definition: A command interpreter that reads input, parses commands and asks the operating system to execute them.

simple_definition: One instruction typed to the shell.
technical_definition: A line of input consisting of a program name followed by options and arguments, executed by the shell.

simple_definition: The text the shell shows when it is waiting for you to type.
technical_definition: A string printed by the shell to indicate readiness for input.

simple_definition: A widely used shell; the one this book uses for its examples.
technical_definition: The Bourne-Again Shell, a Unix command interpreter.

simple_definition: A Bash environment for Windows that is installed with Git for Windows; it is not Git itself.
technical_definition: A terminal providing a Bash shell and Unix-style utilities on Windows, distributed with Git for Windows.
example: The window you open to type Git commands on Windows.

simple_definition: A word that changes how a command behaves.
technical_definition: A command-line parameter, usually prefixed with one or two dashes, that modifies a command's behaviour.

simple_definition: The thing a command acts on, such as a file name.
technical_definition: A value passed to a command on the command line.

simple_definition: A named piece of text the shell remembers.
technical_definition: A named storage location in a shell holding a string value that can be referenced in later commands.

simple_definition: A variable that programs started from the shell can read.
technical_definition: A variable exported into the environment inherited by child processes.

simple_definition: Prints the folder you are currently in.
technical_definition: Print working directory: outputs the absolute path of the current directory.

simple_definition: Creates a new folder.
technical_definition: Make directory: creates directories; -p also creates missing parent directories.

simple_definition: Moves you into another folder.
technical_definition: Change directory: sets the shell's current working directory.

simple_definition: Creates an empty file, or updates a file's last-changed time.
technical_definition: Creates an empty file if it does not exist, or updates its timestamps.

simple_definition: The list of folders the shell searches for programs.
technical_definition: An environment variable containing an ordered list of directories searched to resolve command names. Not to be confused with a file path.
example: A tool in a folder not on PATH gives 'command not found'.

simple_definition: A way of writing formatted text using plain-text marks.
technical_definition: A lightweight markup language whose plain-text syntax is converted to structured documents such as HTML.

simple_definition: A program that turns marked-up text into a formatted result.
technical_definition: Software that parses a markup language and produces a presentation, such as HTML, from it.

simple_definition: A precise written specification of the core Markdown syntax.
technical_definition: A standardised specification of Markdown syntax intended to make different implementations behave consistently.

simple_definition: A copy of your files kept elsewhere so they can be restored after loss.
technical_definition: A duplicate of data stored separately from the original to allow recovery after loss or damage.
example: A nightly copy of a laptop to an external drive.

simple_definition: A folder whose contents are kept the same across computers or an online service.
technical_definition: A directory whose contents are replicated automatically between devices or a service.
example: A folder that appears on your laptop and phone.

simple_definition: One particular state of a file or project at a point in time.
technical_definition: A distinct recorded state of a file or project.
example: The menu as it was on Monday.

simple_definition: The recorded sequence of versions of a project, with reasons and authors.
technical_definition: The ordered record of a project's versions together with metadata such as author, date and description.
example: Every recorded change to the bakery menu.

simple_definition: A system that records a project's history so changes can be seen, reversed and combined.
technical_definition: A system that records changes to files over time, supporting retrieval of earlier versions, comparison, and collaborative work.

simple_definition: A marker that stops others from changing a file until you release it.
technical_definition: A mechanism preventing concurrent modification of a resource by others.

simple_definition: To combine two sets of changes into one.
technical_definition: The operation of integrating changes from two lines of work into a single version.
example: Joining Alice's cake addition and Bob's price change.

simple_definition: A project together with the complete record of its history.
technical_definition: A store containing a project's files and the full history of changes to them; in Git, the project folder plus its .git directory.
example: The sunrise-bakery folder after Git is started in it.

simple_definition: One server holds the only complete history; users hold working copies.
technical_definition: A version-control architecture with a single central repository that clients connect to.
example: A shared server everyone must reach to record work.
related: distributed version control; single point of failure

simple_definition: Every user holds a complete copy of the repository and its history.
technical_definition: A version-control architecture in which each participant has a full repository, and repositories exchange history peer to peer.

simple_definition: A complete copy of a repository, with all its history, made on another computer.
technical_definition: A full copy of a repository including history, produced by cloning.
example: Your copy of a project from a shared server.

simple_definition: A part whose failure stops everything or loses something irreplaceable.
technical_definition: A component in a system whose failure causes the entire system to fail.
example: A single central server with no backup.

simple_definition: A free, open-source version-control system that runs on your computer.
technical_definition: A distributed version-control system that records the history of a project in a repository.
example: The program you use to record versions of sunrise-bakery.

simple_definition: An online service that stores shared repositories and adds collaboration features.
technical_definition: A web service providing remote repository storage and collaboration tools such as issue tracking and review.

simple_definition: A widely used online platform for hosting Git repositories and collaborating on software.
technical_definition: A hosting platform built around Git repositories with collaboration and automation features.

simple_definition: Another hosting platform for Git repositories.
technical_definition: A hosting platform for Git repositories with collaboration and automation features.

simple_definition: Another hosting platform for Git repositories, from a different company.
technical_definition: A hosting platform for Git repositories with collaboration features.
example: A team's repository hosted outside GitHub.

simple_definition: The command that reads and changes Git's settings.
technical_definition: Reads, writes and lists Git configuration values across system, global, local and worktree scopes.

simple_definition: A Git setting that applies to your user account in every repository.
technical_definition: A configuration value stored in the user's global file (~/.gitconfig) and applied to all repositories of that user.

simple_definition: A named value that changes how Git behaves.
technical_definition: A key of the form section.name with a value, read from Git's configuration files, environment and command line.

simple_definition: The level at which a setting is stored: system, global, local or worktree.
technical_definition: The configuration file level (system, global, local, worktree) at which a value is stored, determining its reach and precedence.
example: A local value beats a global one in that repository.

simple_definition: To replace a setting's value for one command or one shell.
technical_definition: To supply a value that takes precedence over stored configuration, for example with git -c or an environment variable.

simple_definition: A complete picture of all the files of a project at one moment.
technical_definition: The state of the tracked files at a point in time, as recorded by a commit's tree.
example: The whole bakery site as it was when you committed.

simple_definition: The folder of files you see and edit.
technical_definition: The checked-out files of a repository on disk, including changes not yet staged or committed.

simple_definition: The holding area that lists exactly what the next commit will contain.
technical_definition: Git's staging area (index): a file in .git recording the content that will form the next commit.

simple_definition: To add a file's current contents to the index so the next commit includes them.
technical_definition: To record a file's current state in the index (git add).

simple_definition: The complete history, kept in the hidden .git folder on your computer.
technical_definition: The .git directory holding a project's objects, references and configuration.

simple_definition: A file Git knows about, because it is in the last commit or in the index.
technical_definition: A file present in the index or in HEAD's tree.

simple_definition: A recorded snapshot with author, time, message and a link to the previous commit; also the action of making one.
technical_definition: A Git object recording a tree, parent commits, author and committer identities, timestamps and a message.

simple_definition: The long code that uniquely identifies a commit.
technical_definition: A cryptographic hash of an object's content, used as its identifier; usually abbreviated.

simple_definition: A movable name that points to a commit.
technical_definition: A reference under refs/heads that holds the identifier of a commit and moves forward with new commits.

simple_definition: The pointer that says which commit you are currently on.
technical_definition: A reference, normally symbolic, to the current branch or commit; the parent of the next commit.

simple_definition: Creates a new repository in the current folder.
technical_definition: Initialises an empty Git repository by creating the .git directory.

simple_definition: Shows which files are untracked, modified or staged, and the current branch.
technical_definition: Reports the state of the working tree and index relative to HEAD; read-only.

simple_definition: Stages files so they are part of the next commit.
technical_definition: Updates the index with the current content of the given paths.

simple_definition: Records the staged snapshot with a message.
technical_definition: Creates a commit object from the index and advances the current branch.

simple_definition: Shows the history of commits, newest first.
technical_definition: Lists commits reachable from the current revision in reverse chronological order, with options for format and filtering.

simple_definition: Any way of naming a commit: a hash, a branch name, HEAD, HEAD~2.
technical_definition: A specifier that resolves to a commit (or other object), as defined by Git's revision syntax.

simple_definition: A report of the differences between two versions, line by line.
technical_definition: A description of changes between two file or tree states, shown as removed (-) and added (+) lines in hunks.

simple_definition: One contiguous chunk of changes in a diff.
technical_definition: A group of adjacent changed lines with context in a unified diff, introduced by an @@ header.

simple_definition: Displays one commit: its message and changes.
technical_definition: Shows a commit's metadata and diff (or other objects).

simple_definition: A file Git has been told to leave alone.
technical_definition: A file matching an ignore pattern that Git omits from untracked listings and from git add of directories.

simple_definition: A text file listing patterns of files Git should ignore.
technical_definition: A file whose lines are patterns (with comments and negations) applied to paths under its directory; normally tracked.

simple_definition: Renames or moves a file and stages the change.
technical_definition: Moves a file in the working tree and index in one operation.

simple_definition: Deletes a file and stages the deletion.
technical_definition: Removes a path from the working tree and the index; with --cached only from the index.

simple_definition: Replaces the last commit with a new one, to fix its message or add forgotten changes.
technical_definition: Creates a new commit from the index and message that replaces the tip commit; the replaced commit is left unreferenced.

simple_definition: A commit containing one logical change.
technical_definition: A commit that is complete and self-contained, with a single purpose, that can be reviewed or reverted independently.

simple_definition: A commit with a message but no file change.
technical_definition: A commit whose tree is identical to its parent's, created with --allow-empty.
example: Mark the start of the spring menu

simple_definition: Lists, creates, renames and deletes branches.
technical_definition: Manages branch references under refs/heads.

simple_definition: Changes the current branch.
technical_definition: Moves HEAD to another branch and updates the index and working tree to match.

simple_definition: HEAD points directly at a commit instead of a branch.
technical_definition: A state in which HEAD contains a commit identifier rather than a symbolic reference to a branch.

simple_definition: A merge that only moves a branch pointer forward.
technical_definition: A merge in which the receiving branch has not diverged, so Git moves its pointer to the source commit and creates no merge commit.

simple_definition: Each branch has commits the other lacks.
technical_definition: Two branches have diverged when neither tip is an ancestor of the other, so a fast-forward is impossible.
example: Hours added on main while tea is added on add-tea.

simple_definition: A commit that joins two lines of work.
technical_definition: A commit with two or more parents, recording where lines of work were combined.

simple_definition: Turn many commits into one.
technical_definition: Combine the changes of several commits into a single new commit, leaving no link to the originals.

simple_definition: Git cannot combine two changes by itself.
technical_definition: A situation in which both sides changed the same part of a file differently, so Git stops the merge and asks the user to decide.
example: Two branches set the white loaf price differently.

simple_definition: The lines Git writes into a conflicted file.
technical_definition: The <<<<<<<, ======= and >>>>>>> lines that delimit the two versions; all must be removed before committing.

simple_definition: A repository with no working files, used as a shared hub.
technical_definition: A repository holding only Git's database, with no checked-out working tree; the form used for shared remotes.

simple_definition: Your note of where a remote branch was when you last looked.
technical_definition: A read-only local reference such as origin/main that Git updates on fetch, pull and push.

simple_definition: The remote branch a local branch follows.
technical_definition: The branch named by branch.<name>.remote and branch.<name>.merge, used by plain push, pull and status.

simple_definition: Download new commits without changing your branches.
technical_definition: Retrieve objects and update remote-tracking branches, leaving local branches and the working tree untouched.

simple_definition: Fetch, then merge into your current branch.
technical_definition: git fetch followed by integrating the upstream branch into the current branch, by default with a merge.

simple_definition: A shelf for unfinished changes.
technical_definition: A stack of saved working-tree and index states that lets you return to a clean tree and reapply the changes later.

simple_definition: A fixed name for one commit.
technical_definition: A reference that names a commit and, unlike a branch, does not move when new commits are made.

simple_definition: A tag that is just a name.
technical_definition: A tag that is only a reference to a commit, with no tagger, date or message of its own.

simple_definition: A tag with a message and tagger.
technical_definition: A tag stored as its own object with tagger, date and message; the usual choice for releases.
